knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A test patch shows how the stone responds to the proposed method before the full area is treated.
The test record needs the method, the abrasive or product, the water use, the contact time, the result and the location.
Dusting in a test means the controls are missing. Stop, add the wet method or extraction, and repeat the test.
Cracks and loose edges can break under a grinder or pad, which creates dust and a hazard.
A passing test shows the response of the surface to a method. It does not identify the material.

practicalCriteria: Completes the assessment sheet with dated photographs
Runs the test patch with the same controls as the full job
Records the test with method, result and location
Decides to proceed, change or stop, and records the decision
passRule: Knowledge checks: 4 of 5 correct (80%). Practical sign-off is separate and is not granted by the knowledge check: an assessor must observe every critical practical criterion and record it.
evidenceRequired: Test patch log with method, result and location
stopWorkCriteria: Surface that cannot be identified as natural stone or terrazzo
Test patch damages the surface beyond what the method can manage
A crack or loose edge would be affected by the method
